record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
record.context_brief: Hadronic final states in CCQE-like models
record.original_question: How can neutrino-nucleus CCQE-like interaction models that reproduce outgoing charged-lepton kinematics also assign a hadronic final state consistently, including outgoing proton multiplicities and kinematics, for fine-grained tracking detectors and liquid-argon time projection chambers?

evidence.quote:
While impressive agreement is achieved in the outgoing lepton kinematics
observed in the MiniBooNE CCQE data by the RPA-based calculations,
the ability to predict the corresponding hadronic component of the inter-
action remains a challenge. With availability of data from ﬁne grained
detectors (NOMAD, MINERvA, ND280) and LAr TPCs capable of re-
solving the detailed ﬁnal state of CCQE interactions (ArgoNeuT, Micro-
BooNE), including outgoing proton multiplicities and kinematics, it will
be important to ﬁnd a suitable means of consistently assigning a predicted
hadronic state with the lepton kinematics in an event.

From the various theoretical approaches presented at the workshop, there
seems to be convergence on the characterization of the multi-nucleon eﬀects in
the inclusive CCQE process, where the process is considered integrating over
possible hadronic ﬁnal states. However, the current and upcoming suite of neu-
trino experiments utilizing ﬁne grained tracking detectors and LAr-TPCs will
demand a more exclusive description of the CCQE process in order to inter-
pret their data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider charged-current quasi-elastic-like (CCQE-like) neutrino–nucleus scattering, in which an incoming neutrino interacts with a nucleus (e.g. carbon or argon) producing an outgoing charged lepton together with one or more knocked-out nucleons, in the kinematic regime relevant to accelerator-based neutrino experiments (incoming neutrino energies of order 0.5–5 GeV). Theoretical descriptions of this process commonly include single-nucleon quasi-elastic scattering supplemented by random-phase-approximation (RPA) corrections, multi-nucleon (2p2h/np-nh) contributions, and final-state interactions of the outgoing hadrons in the nuclear medium.

Such inclusive descriptions, which integrate over hadronic final states, can reproduce the measured outgoing charged-lepton kinematics (for example double-differential cross sections in the muon momentum and angle). However, fine-grained tracking detectors and liquid-argon time projection chambers are able to resolve the exclusive hadronic final state, including the multiplicity of outgoing protons above detection threshold and their individual momenta and angles.

Problem: Construct a theoretical and computational framework for CCQE-like neutrino–nucleus interactions that simultaneously
(i) reproduces the inclusive outgoing charged-lepton double-differential kinematics with the same accuracy as current RPA + multi-nucleon inclusive calculations, and
(ii) consistently assigns, on an event-by-event basis, an exclusive hadronic final state — specifying the number of outgoing protons above a given kinematic threshold and their full momentum distributions — that is correlated with the lepton kinematics in a manner derived from the underlying nuclear dynamics (rather than imposed by an ad hoc cascade) and that agrees with exclusive proton-multiplicity and proton-kinematics measurements from fine-grained tracking detectors and liquid-argon time projection chambers.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g. relativistic distorted-wave impulse approximation implementations in NEUT, 2025; MicroBooNE final-state-interaction studies on argon, 2024) continues to develop and benchmark exclusive CCQE-like models with proton multiplicities and kinematics, but no single framework has been established that simultaneously reproduces inclusive lepton kinematics and exclusive hadronic final states across carbon and argon targets. The problem of consistently assigning the hadronic final state with the lepton kinematics remains an active area of investigation.

status_evidence.title: Implementation of a relativistic distorted wave impulse approximation model into NEUT
status_evidence.snippet: Final state interactions, both elastic and inelastic, are modelled by combining distorted waves with NEUT's intranuclear cascade ... benchmarked against νµ-¹²C and νµ-⁴⁰Ar measurements.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work is still developing and benchmarking exclusive hadronic-final-state models for CCQE — indicating the consistent assignment problem is not yet fully solved.

status_evidence.title: Final-state interactions in neutrino-induced proton knockout from argon in MicroBooNE
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of proton knockout in MicroBooNE constrain final-state interaction models on argon.
status_evidence.claim: Exclusive proton kinematics on argon remain an active subject of model–data comparison, supporting the open status.
